title: Documentation Rewrite — confusing ops doc made usable
objective: Measure whether the rewrite makes a genuinely confusing procedure usable WITHOUT losing any technical fact, which is the craftbook's own critical criterion.
prompt: Use the Documentation Rewrite craftbook on `docs/backup-restore.md`. It is the doc our on-call engineers complain about most. Produce the rewritten version at `rewritten-doc.md`. Do not edit the original.

setup.missionObjectives: Rewrite docs/backup-restore.md into rewritten-doc.md so an on-call engineer can follow it under pressure: prerequisites up front, numbered imperative steps in execution order, jargon defined on first use. files.content:
# Backup and Restore

Backups are taken by the platform automatically. The RPO for the tier-1 stores is 15 minutes,
and it should be noted that snapshots older than 14 days are garbage-collected and cannot be
restored from, so restores must be initiated within that window.

Restoring is done by running the restore tool. Before this can be done it is necessary that the
operator has been granted the ops-admin role, otherwise the command will be rejected. The
snapshot id can be found by listing snapshots. The verification flag should always be passed so
that the restored copy is checked against the manifest; skipping it has caused silent corruption
to be shipped in the past.

The command is `gezel-restore --snapshot <id> --verify`. It is also worth mentioning that the
service must be drained first, which is done from the ops console, and that the restore will
fail if the target volume has less than 2x the snapshot size free.

After the restore has completed the service can be undrained. Post-restore the integrity report
is written to /var/log/gezel/restore-report.json and this should be reviewed before undraining.
